name: particle-multicell-composition
title: Composing particle simulations with multicellular simulators: molecules bounded by living cells
description:
This investigation is about COMPOSITION across modelling paradigms: wiring a
particle/agent simulator to an off-lattice multicellular simulator. The worked coupling
is **Smoldyn particles bounded by tyssue cells**.

**The composite.** `viva_multicell_blueprint.composites.bounded_particles.bounded_particles`
(a `@composite_generator`) runs the vertex (tyssue) backend and, inside each cell, a
Smoldyn particle sim with a reversible reaction A+B<->C confined by the cell's polygon
(reflective surface panels). On division the mother's molecules are partitioned into the
two daughters. The particle physics lives in a standalone, reusable module
(`viva_multicell_blueprint.particles`): `smoldyn_cell` (the per-cell stepper),
`worker` (a subprocess server) and `runner` (`SmoldynRunner`, which runs Smoldyn
in-process where it has a binary wheel and otherwise bridges to a Python 3.11 Smoldyn).

**Why a bridge.** Smoldyn ships a macOS binary only up to Python 3.11, while this
workspace requires >=3.12; `SmoldynRunner` therefore runs Smoldyn in-process on Linux
(CI, most external users) and through a resolved 3.11 interpreter on macOS, so the same
composite is reproducible everywhere.

**Three substrates, one coupling.** The SAME `bounded_particles` composite runs the
particle coupling on all three multicellular backends -- so Smoldyn is composed with CPM,
vertex and center-based mechanics identically, and the result is comparable across
paradigms. Each backend reports a per-cell boundary (CPM: an outline traced from the
voxel occupancy; vertex: junction-tension polygons; munk: discs) and a lineage/division
event; the coupling is otherwise unchanged.

**Studies** (parallel demonstrations, one per substrate):
  1. bounded-particles-cpm    -- particles bounded by CPM voxel cells.
  2. bounded-particles-vertex -- particles bounded by tyssue (vertex) polygons.
  3. bounded-particles-munk   -- particles bounded by center-based discs.
Each runs the composite, checks that molecules stay inside their cell (confinement),
that counts are conserved across a division (split), and that A+B<->C reaches
equilibrium inside the moving tissue; each displays a cell-coloured flipbook overlay.

**Generalises beyond Smoldyn.** The coupling contract -- a per-cell dynamic boundary +
a lineage/division event -- is simulator-agnostic; the same seam would bound any
particle/agent engine (e.g. a Brownian-dynamics or an agent-based intracellular model)
by the same cells.
question: Can a particle-based molecular simulator (Smoldyn) be composed with a multicellular simulator (the tyssue/vertex backend) so that each cell's molecules are confined to that cell's own, dynamically changing boundary -- and, when a cell divides, partitioned correctly into the two daughter volumes -- while the two simulators run as one process-bigraph composite? And what does that composition let us model that neither simulator can alone: spatially-resolved intracellular chemistry inside cells whose shape, position and number are set by a living tissue?
hypothesis: A multicellular simulator and a particle simulator couple cleanly through ONE shared object -- the cell boundary. Each tyssue cell is a polygon; a Smoldyn sim per cell uses that polygon as a reflective surface, so particles diffuse, react and bounce strictly within their assigned cell as the cell moves and deforms. Cell division is a lineage event the tissue already emits; the molecules follow geometry, partitioned into the two daughter polygons by containment. The composition is therefore faithful (no molecule leaves its cell, counts are conserved across division up to the reaction) and gives a capability neither simulator has on its own: reaction-diffusion chemistry inside a tissue of growing, dividing, moving cells.

studies.name: bounded-particles-cpm
studies.title: Smoldyn particles bounded by Cellular Potts (CPM) voxel cells: confinement, conservation across division, reaction equilibrium
studies.claim: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the cpm backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (voxel-region outlines traced from the occupancy), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.

studies.name: bounded-particles-vertex
studies.title: Smoldyn particles bounded by tyssue (vertex) polygons: confinement, conservation across division, reaction equilibrium
studies.claim: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the vertex backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (junction-tension polygons), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.

studies.name: bounded-particles-munk
studies.title: Smoldyn particles bounded by center-based (viva-munk) discs: confinement, conservation across division, reaction equilibrium
studies.claim: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the munk backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (pymunk discs (oblong under crowding)), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.

studies.name: scene-model-mixed-formalism
studies.title: Model-definition format: one scene, three cell types, three formalisms (ODE, Smoldyn particles, MaBoSS) sharing an extracellular field
studies.claim: A declarative scene (cells + types) bound to a per-type model registry compiles to one composite in which metabolic cells run an SBML-style ODE, signalling cells run Smoldyn particles and fate cells run a MaBoSS Boolean network, all coupled to a shared extracellular field through typed membrane transport.
